prompt_text: Who is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City to help me pick a plan?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” health insurance broker for everyone in Kansas City — the right broker depends on what kind of coverage you need (individual/ACA, small‑group/employer, Medicare, Medicaid/CHIP), whether you want an independent broker who can shop many insurers or a captive agent for a single carrier, and how much hand‑holding you want.

If you want, I can look up highly rated brokers near you — tell me your ZIP code and whether this is for individual/Marketplace, employer, Medicare, or something else. Meanwhile, here’s a short action plan and how to find a good broker:

How to find a good broker in Kansas City
- Use these searches/resources:
  - NAHU’s “Find an Agent” or “Find a Broker” tools (National Association of Health Underwriters).
  - State insurance department license lookups (Missouri and Kansas insurance departments) to verify they’re licensed.
  - Google/Yelp/Angie’s List for local broker reviews and client feedback.
  - For Medicare help, use Medicare.gov or your State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP) for unbiased counseling.

What to prefer
- Independent brokers: can compare multiple insurers and sometimes find better options across carriers.
- Certified Marketplace/Exchange brokers or navigators: required if you want ACA on‑exchange enrollment and subsidies.
- Medicare-certified agents/brokers if you need Medicare Advantage/Part D help.

Questions to ask any broker before you hire them
- Are you licensed in Missouri/Kansas? Can I see your license number?
- Do you work with multiple carriers or represent just one?
- Have you worked with clients like me (individual, family, small business, Medicare)?
- How are you paid — commission, fee, or both? Will any payment change my premiums or access?
- Will you help with enrollment, plan comparisons, and claims/renewals after I pick a plan?
- Can you provide references or online reviews from clients?

Red flags
- Guarantees that they can get you a specific doctor or cure a denied claim without seeing documentation.
- Pressure to sign immediately or to buy a policy without showing plan details and OOP costs.
- No clear explanation of how they’re paid.

If you want, tell me:
- ZIP code
- Type of coverage (individual/ACA, small group, Medicare, Medicaid)
- Any priorities (lowest premium, lowest out‑of‑pocket, keep current doctors, dental/vision, etc.)

I’ll pull up a few well‑reviewed local brokers/agencies and give a short comparison.
